questions.question: Which JavaScript method opens an HTML5 <dialog> as a true modal with focus trapping and backdrop?
questions.explanation: showModal() opens the dialog as a modal in the Top Layer, activates keyboard focus trapping, and displays the ::backdrop.

questions.question: Which element combination creates a native collapsible disclosure widget with zero JavaScript?
questions.explanation: <details> and <summary> provide built-in collapsible disclosures natively in modern browsers.

questions.question: What is the behavior of content placed inside a <template> element?
options: It is rendered immediately with low opacity
It is inert and not rendered or executed until cloned via JavaScript
It automatically submits to the server
It creates a web worker thread
questions.hint: Template contents are inert until cloned.
questions.explanation: <template> content is not rendered upon page load; it serves as client-side HTML to be cloned dynamically by scripts.

questions.question: How can you make a <details> disclosure open by default when the page loads?
options: Add the boolean attribute open: <details open>
questions.explanation: The 'open' boolean attribute on <details> sets its initial state to expanded.

questions.question: What happens when a user presses the Escape (Esc) key while a dialog opened with showModal() is active?
questions.hint: Native Esc key handling in modals.
questions.explanation: HTML5 modal dialogs natively handle the Esc key to dismiss the dialog without requiring custom keydown listeners.
